paper_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
claim: LoRA reduces the number of trainable parameters by 10,000x and GPU memory requirement by 3x compared to GPT-3 175B fine-tuned with Adam.
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract states this directly with both numbers.

paper_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
claim: LoRA performs on-par or better than full fine-tuning in model quality on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2, and GPT-3, despite far fewer trainable parameters.
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract states LoRA performs on-par or better across all four models; results tables (e.g. WikiSQL, GPT-3 tasks) support this.

paper_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
claim: LoRA freezes the pretrained weights and only trains small rank-decomposition matrices (W0 + delta W = W0 + BA, with W0 frozen and A, B trainable).
ground_truth_evidence: Method section explicitly defines this formulation.

paper_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
claim: Deploying independently fine-tuned GPT-3 175B instances for each task is prohibitively expensive.
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract and introduction state this as the core motivation.

paper_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
claim: QLoRA can finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance.
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract states this directly.

paper_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
claim: Guanaco (QLoRA's best model) reaches 99.3% of ChatGPT's performance level on the Vicuna benchmark after 24 hours of finetuning on a single GPU.
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract states this; Table 6 confirms Guanaco 65B at 99.3%.

paper_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
claim: Guanaco 7B needs ~5GB deployed and outperforms a 26GB Alpaca model by more than 20 percentage points.
ground_truth_evidence: Prose states 5GB and >20pp vs a 26GB Alpaca model, matching the claim. Note: Table 6 lists Alpaca 13B as 10GB with 69.4% vs Guanaco 7B 87.9%, an internal inconsistency between the paper's prose (26GB) and its own table (10GB) for the same comparison.
notes: verified by direct reading; paper has an internal prose-vs-table inconsistency, worth noting as a limitation/edge case for the fact-checker

paper_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
claim: QLoRA introduces NF4 (4-bit NormalFloat), Double Quantization, and Paged Optimizers as its three key memory-saving innovations.
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract explicitly lists all three; Double Quantization detailed as saving ~0.37 bits/parameter (~3GB for 65B model).

paper_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
claim: Guanaco 33B uses 21GB vs 26GB for Vicuna 13B and outperforms it by about 3 percentage points.
ground_truth_evidence: Prose states 21GB vs 26GB and ~3pp improvement; Table 6 gives 97.8% vs 94.9% (2.9pp, rounds to 3.0).

paper_title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
claim: Standard LoRA is suboptimal for models with large width (embedding dimension) because its adapter matrices A and B are updated with the same learning rate, which prevents efficient feature learning.
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract and introduction/theory establish this directly.

paper_title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
claim: LoRA+ corrects this by setting different learning rates for adapter matrices A and B, using a well-chosen fixed ratio (eta_B = lambda * eta_A, with fixed lambda > 1).
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract states the correction; later formalized with the eta_B = lambda*eta_A relation.

paper_title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
claim: LoRA+ improves performance by 1-2% and finetuning speed by up to ~2x compared to standard LoRA, at the same computational cost.
ground_truth_evidence: Stated almost verbatim in the abstract.

paper_title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
claim: DistilBERT reduces BERT's size by 40%, retains 97% of its language understanding capabilities, and is 60% faster.
ground_truth_evidence: Stated directly in the abstract.

paper_title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
claim: DistilBERT uses a triple loss combining language modeling loss, distillation loss, and cosine-distance loss during pre-training.
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract introduces the triple loss; Method section explains the three components.

paper_title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
claim: On IMDb sentiment classification, DistilBERT is only about 0.6 percentage points behind full BERT while being 40% smaller.
ground_truth_evidence: Table 2: BERT-base 93.46% vs DistilBERT 92.82% (0.64pp diff, described as 0.6pp).

paper_title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
claim: On SQuAD v1.1, DistilBERT stays within 3.9 points of full BERT's performance.
ground_truth_evidence: Stated directly; Table 2 gives BERT 81.2/88.5 EM/F1 vs DistilBERT 77.7/85.8.

paper_title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
claim: Unlike most prior work which applied distillation only for task-specific models, DistilBERT applies knowledge distillation during the pre-training phase.
ground_truth_evidence: Abstract and Related Work explicitly contrast this with prior task-specific distillation approaches.

paper_title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
claim: ALBERT introduces two parameter-reduction techniques to lower BERT's memory consumption and increase training speed.
ground_truth_evidence: Stated directly in the abstract.

paper_title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
claim: ALBERT's best model achieves new state-of-the-art results on GLUE, RACE, and SQuAD benchmarks while having fewer parameters than BERT-large.
ground_truth_evidence: Stated directly in the abstract.

paper_title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
claim: ALBERT-xxlarge has only about 70% of BERT-large's parameters (233/235M vs 334M) yet shows significant improvements over BERT-large on SQuAD 1.1, SQuAD 2.0, MNLI, SST-2, and RACE.
ground_truth_evidence: Confirmed against parameter counts and per-task improvement figures in the paper.

paper_title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
claim: ALBERT pushes RACE accuracy to 89.4%, the GLUE benchmark score to 89.4, and SQuAD 2.0 test F1 to 92.2.
ground_truth_evidence: Explicitly reported in text and benchmark tables.

paper_title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
claim: ALBERT uses a self-supervised Sentence Order Prediction (SOP) loss focused on inter-sentence coherence, which consistently helps downstream tasks with multi-sentence inputs.
ground_truth_evidence: Technical substance confirmed: SOP targets inter-sentence coherence and shows consistent gains on multi-sentence tasks. Correction noted: Section 3 frames ALBERT as having three main contributions (factorized embedding parameterization, cross-layer parameter sharing, and SOP) rather than SOP being simply the 'second' contribution.
notes: verified by direct reading; minor framing correction applied
